sections.heading: Roof Repair or Roof Replacement? The 25% Rule and NJ Permits for West Orange Homes

c.v: Many roof problems do not require immediate replacement.

runs.v: Roof repairs typically include leak fixes and flashing replacements, and an honest assessment weighs condition, not age alone: asphalt shingles typically last 20 to 30 years, yet a roof that has served West Orange winters for 20 years may still repair well. Local property-maintenance codes generally require roofs to be kept watertight, so repair or replace before water gets in.

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: Once damage covers more than about 25% of the roof, replacement usually makes more sense than another repair, and roof replacement is often necessary when damage is widespread. In New Jersey, repairing more than 25% of the roof area within 12 months also needs a permit on any building but a detached one- or two-family home, under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.

c.v: Do I need a permit to replace my roof in NJ?

runs.v: Under the NJ Uniform Construction Code, a complete roof replacement needs a permit on most buildings; re-roofing a detached one- or two-family house is the exception, classed as ordinary maintenance. Confirm with the West Orange construction office before work.

A roof replacement in West Orange typically ranges from $8,000 to $30,000, against a New Jersey residential average of about $4,500 to $16,500, and most residential replacements take one to two days. Options include metal roofing, which withstands severe weather well, and slate, prized for durability and appearance. GAF and Owens Corning offer manufacturer warranties of up to 50 years on premium shingle systems; Newark Quality Roofing backs its labor with a written workmanship warranty and ends every job with a magnet sweep for nails.

faqs.q: How often should I have my West Orange roof inspected?

runs.v: The NRCA recommends a roof inspection at least twice per year, spring and fall, plus an additional inspection after any major weather event; at a minimum, annual roof inspections catch small issues before they escalate. A West Orange home near South Mountain or Eagle Rock Reservation benefits from a post-leaf-drop check, because reservation-edge debris hides condition in valleys and gutters.

faqs.q: Do you inspect slate and copper roofs on Llewellyn Park estates?

runs.v: Yes. A Newark Quality Roofing inspection of a Llewellyn Park estate or hillside Tudor checks fasteners and copper flashing, because natural slate rarely fails as a tile, instead failing at corroded fasteners and degraded flashing, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart. NPS Preservation Brief 29 advises replacing the roof rather than individual slates once 20% or more are broken, cracked, missing, or sliding.

faqs.q: Does a roof inspection need a permit or historic approval in West Orange?

runs.v: No. A roof inspection itself requires no permit, and a detached one- or two-family reroof counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. Before exterior work on a designated landmark or a home in a historic district, confirm requirements with the West Orange construction office, because those properties can need extra review; per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private owner.

faqs.q: Can a roof inspection find a leak before it appears inside?

runs.v: Yes. A roof inspection finds a leak before it appears inside by measuring deck and framing moisture with moisture meters and locating trapped moisture with infrared imaging, so a failing flashing or membrane detail is caught while the repair stays minor on West Orange's ridge-side and commercial roofs.
